claims.text: Alloying an elemental Cr coating with Al, Ti, Ni, and Ta will reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
An AlTiCrNiTa coating will have greater oxidation resistance than an elemental Cr coating.
The modified coating will improve cladding durability in both approximately 300 °C subcritical water and approximately 1200 °C steam.
The alloying additions will produce a stable, adherent reactive-element oxide layer.
The reactive-element oxide layer will act as a diffusion barrier that limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion at the coating–substrate interface.
The added Al, Ti, Ni, and Ta will promote formation of a protective oxide scale in high-temperature steam.
The protective scale will lower oxidation in high-temperature steam.
The protective oxide will create a chemical barrier that mitigates diffusion of Cr into the zirconium alloy.
The modified coating will retain coating integrity better than elemental Cr across both service regimes.
The modified coating will exhibit lower oxidation rates than the elemental Cr baseline.
The modified coating will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than the elemental Cr baseline.
The modified coating will maintain mechanical integrity better than the elemental Cr baseline.
Elemental Cr coatings perform acceptably in either service regime but fail prematurely when exposed to both regimes.
Enhanced interfacial interdiffusion causes the premature failure of the elemental Cr baseline.
